title: Context Assembly and Citation: Visual Guide
outline: Title: Context Assembly and Citation — Visual Guide (IR 301, lesson 02)

1. From Chunks To Prompt | The bridge from lesson 01: an overlap slider (0-250 of 500 tokens) shows stride, index inflation and the tokens of verbatim repetition, and a toggle flips the reranked top-8 between 'as retrieved' and 'after deduplication', collapsing A5-A8 and B2-B3 into merged spans and promoting ranks 9-12. | Overlap chosen at index time is paid for again in the context window: four documents wearing eight slots, with the second-best source (the wholesale refund policy) omitted entirely until you deduplicate.

2. Select And Order | A lambda slider drives greedy MMR over 6 candidates with the round-by-round arithmetic printed (lambda x sim minus (1-lambda) x max-similarity-to-selected), and below it a context-size slider (3-20) plus three ordering strategies lay the picks on a U-shaped attention curve and compute the percentage of evidence weight surviving. | Below lambda ~0.89 the second pick flips from retail to wholesale so the comparison gets both sides; ordering barely matters at 3-5 chunks and decides the answer at 20, where 'grouped by document' can drop the strongest evidence into the dead middle.

3. Verify The Quote | Six generated sentences with markers and quoted spans, checked under three verifiers (markers only / exact string match / normalized match); tapping a row explains its case, and pills count accepted, rejected, wrong labels shipped and false rejections. | A marker is a claim about a claim; only matching the span against the chunk it names catches [3] cited for text that lives in [7] — and a matched quote still proves existence, not support.

4. Pre-Filter Or Post | A pass-rate slider (5-100%) with a pre-filter/post-filter toggle shows k=10 wanted against survivors and the k/p overfetch needed, and a four-rung relaxation ladder walks the Initech example from three filters and 0 hits down to the locked system defaults. | Post-filtering turns a 20% pass rate into 2 chunks and answers from starvation unless you overfetch k/p = 50; inferred filters are the first rung down the ladder and tenant/status defaults are never a rung at all.

5. Density Over Volume | The budget arithmetic (8000 - 600 - 400 - 100 - 1500 = 5400 tokens = 13 chunks) sits above a k slider (1-20) that recomputes relevance density, answer quality and linear input cost, with the reranker score row 0.92 / 0.88 / 0.85 / 0.41 / 0.39 marking where dynamic k stops. | Quality rises, plateaus and declines while cost rises linearly forever, so the 13-chunk ceiling is not a target: admit while candidates clear the relevance bar, and check density before you check k.
